entries.title: Kyrien: Biography
entries.subtitle: Independent operator and later MSF director
entries.text: Kyrien: Biography Independent operator and later MSF director Kyrien begins the story as an independent figure and the son of a Narvean military commanding officer. His father introduces him to weapons and officer conduct unusually early. At five, Kyrien is allowed to hold a Sparrow and immediately aims it at a civilian in the street. His father stops and scolds him, making clear that familiarity with a weapon never permits a breach of protocol. The incident leaves Kyrien with a quiet affinity for military practice and the moral burden attached to force. After his father's death, he retains that mentality alongside access to surviving contacts, suppliers, knowledge, and tools. The inheritance later enables his attempt on a politician involved in causing his father's death. The target is under MSF protection. The attempt fails because the politician belongs to the Magi world, and Kyrien never learns that Lynleit was present and almost harmed by his actions. Within the first few chapters, the failed attempt ends with Lynleit interrogating Kyrien at a police office. She invokes an extraordinary transfer clause in MSF's government service contract, drafted under Fionn for extraordinary threats, taking control of the case and offering conditional freedom: become her secret helper and remain confined to her demands. Kyrien cannot account for the personal edge in her questioning because Lynleit never tells him what happened. The contract authority shaped under Fionn lets his daughter recruit a man she deliberately hides from him. She wants a deniable trump card against Helena and eventually tells only Felix and Reiner. The coerced arrangement drags him deeper into the world of Magi and gradually into MSF. Reiner remains suspicious but accepts Lynleit's judgment. Felix never fully trusts him and repeatedly clashes with him, leaving Kyrien inside a circle whose members protect Lynleit from him as much as they protect him for her. Short card games after the failed river watches expose Kyrien's private need to win. He usually wins through technical play, while Lynleit learns his stopped breath before a risk and turns his own attention toward her hands, gaze, and stillness. During the fifth watch, he briefly steadies her near the concealed Sparrow when an empty boat shifts. After the river separates him from the team, he witnesses her forbidden water walking and protects the secret. Father Mikhail later exposes the witness breach, and Kyrien refuses to preserve Lynleit's convenient half-truth about Felix and Reiner. While Lynleit is sent to Cardiff, she assigns Kyrien to protect Myka undercover at the Magi Academy. He depends on conventional field skills and communications with Felix and Reiner until the danger exceeds Lynleit's estimate and Natalia intervenes personally. The operation becomes his first sustained experience inside Magi education and Myka's first experience with him and MSF. When Lynleit finally asks why he keeps accepting danger without any reward waiting for him, he answers without hesitation: "Because there's a battle to be fought." He treats the fight itself as sufficient reward. The answer leaves open whether he is proving himself to his own standards or still measuring himself against his dead father. After Helena frames Lynleit and launches the hunt for her arrest, Kyrien gives her refuge and helps her find secure ways to contact the two officers. His hidden position becomes the first practical base of her campaign to reclaim MSF. When Lynleit's institutional authority can no longer enforce their original bargain, Kyrien receives a real opportunity to leave and chooses to remain in the counteroffensive. The decision makes his loyalty voluntary before their relationship becomes sexual. After Fionn's death, Lynleit eventually inherits the Magiarchate as Narvea's new Magiarch. While that office keeps her away from MSF, Kyrien inherits the director's seat, despite being a non-Magus who began as an unofficial asset hidden from Fionn. He must hold together a private company, its government contracts, its divided loyalties, and its permanent mandate against the Spill while the person who connects MSF to the hidden magical order is absent. He survives by reaching the peak of MSF's intelligence-operative side, learning to make decisions without Lynleit's intuition or magical authority and to keep both ordinary intelligence work and Magi-focused containment functioning at once. Lynleit later begins appearing around missions, while Kyrien remains unaware that they have a son. Outside the System Alliance under Pressure The Battle as Reward Undercover at the Academy One Curse across Two Identities The Director without Magecraft The Secret Kept from Him Kyrien

entries.title: Kyrien: Connections
entries.subtitle: Independent operator and later MSF director
entries.text: Kyrien: Connections Independent operator and later MSF director Lynleit Handler and eventual partner She questions him knowing that his failed attack nearly harmed her, a fact he never learns. Their repeated card games create a voluntary contest inside the coerced arrangement. He later protects her water-walking secret, gives her refuge, and chooses to remain once her authority can no longer compel him. Near the end of Arc 1, one curse binds their identities after they destroy a Holumn together. Lynleit initiates their first sexual encounter without revealing the proposed cure, and Kyrien responds deliberately once he understands what she is asking. Their reciprocal change fractures the curse. Kyrien's father Formative authority A military commanding officer who introduces Kyrien to weapons, protocol, and officer morality. His correction of Kyrien's first reckless act with a Sparrow becomes the foundation of his son's belief that using force also means accepting reciprocal danger. Myka Undercover charge Kyrien keeps Myka safe inside the Magi Academy through conventional field skills and contact with Felix and Reiner until Natalia reaches them. Lynleit She begins as his coercive handler and privately knows that his attack almost harmed her. Card games after the failed river watches expose the tells each normally conceals. He later protects her water-walking secret, shelters her after Fionn's murder, and chooses to remain once her authority can no longer compel him. Near the end of Arc 1, their joint destruction of a Holumn binds one fatal curse to both identities. Kyrien knows the prognosis but not Lynleit's proposed answer. He notices her unusual behavior, asks about the curse without forcing an explanation, and deliberately answers her initiative. Their reciprocal change fractures the curse. Tien A shadow operator whose methods mirror Kyrien's skills without his restraint, forcing him to sharpen every discipline that keeps him alive. Potential sexual tension Lynleit Established arc Mutual, slow to surface Kyrien enters Lynleit's interrogation without knowing that his attack on the protected politician almost harmed her. Later, the card games expose his need to win and make him aware that she is studying his breath, hands, and pauses rather than only his play. When asked why he keeps risking himself, he says the battle itself is enough. The answer is honest but incomplete: her elegance, authority, and nerve have become physically distracting before he permits himself to call the reaction desire. His strongest answer remains behavioral, including his deliberate response when she finally crosses the boundary between them. Their attraction begins through observation rather than romance. The interrogation gives Lynleit private knowledge Kyrien cannot read. The failed river watches then give them a voluntary contest outside the handler-asset bargain: Lynleit learns the stopped breath before one of his risks, while he learns the hand movement before one of her decisions. Hands, breath, gaze, pauses, proximity, and competitive attention become their private language. The river recovery and the hotel refuge remain non-sexual thresholds in which restraint makes physical and emotional trust possible. Kyrien's choice to remain after Lynleit's authority loses practical force separates desire from compliance. When a shared Holumn curse later reduces their remaining time to days, Lynleit investigates intimacy as a possible identity change and initiates a clumsy, sudden, almost argumentative encounter. Kyrien understands what she is asking and answers deliberately. The curse does not create their attachment or make sex curative. It forces both to acknowledge a relationship already capable of changing the identities it recognizes. Potential sexual tension Sherie Strong potential Situational and confrontational Sherie's charm is too deliberate to disarm him, but the precision behind it earns his attention. He is more likely to watch for the moment her performance fails than reward the performance itself. Sherie uses language and calibrated flirtation to control the rhythm of an exchange. Kyrien answers with silence, literalism, or no usable reaction at all. Repeated negotiation could turn her professional frustration into sexual tension without making them compatible or displacing Kyrien's eventual relationship with Lynleit. Kyrien

entries.title: Kyrien: Strengths and weaknesses
entries.subtitle: Independent operator and later MSF director
entries.text: Kyrien: Strengths and weaknesses Independent operator and later MSF director Kyrien speaks little and smiles less, yet he is intensely competitive. Cards, chess, an investigation, and a gunfight can all become contests he feels compelled to win. He accepts hard play, but reacts quickly when an opponent cheats, and that urge to punish unfairness can pull him away from the safer objective. He notices when another person behaves against their own pattern, asks directly, and respects a refusal to explain. His clearest answers usually arrive through deliberate action. Intelligence tradecraft 97 He turns surveillance, deception, logistics, human behavior, and escape planning into a substitute for magical perception. Strategic adaptation 94 His practical reasoning converts unfamiliar threats into usable procedures, leverage, and decisions that survive contact with reality. Survival discipline 92 He does not try to overpower Magi. He stays difficult to locate, corner, deceive, or kill. ISTP / INTJ Ti or Ni; ISTP lean Provisional Kyrien

entries.title: Kyrien: Tradecraft
entries.subtitle: Independent operator and later MSF director
entries.text: Kyrien: Tradecraft Independent operator and later MSF director Concealment Subterfuge Controls what others can infer about his intent, identity, loyalties, and next movement. He survives by giving opponents a convincing answer that is not the true one. Escape discipline Evasion Breaks surveillance, avoids magical attention, plans exits before entry, and refuses confrontations whose terms were chosen by somebody else. Misdirection Trickery Uses false patterns, staged weaknesses, timing, and selective truth to make stronger opponents commit to the wrong interpretation. Relative strength Obstacle movement His strength is most effective against his own body weight. He may not strike with the greatest force, but he moves quickly through difficult ground, pulls himself over obstacles, and can climb fences or walls when an escape route demands it. Preparedness Redundant options Kyrien usually keeps at least two objects available that are weapons or can become weapons. The pair changes with circumstance and may include a knife, keys, a pen, or a pocket pistol. The habit keeps options within reach rather than imposing a fixed loadout. Reciprocal force Firearms His father taught him that pointing a weapon creates an obligation. Kyrien keeps the lesson as a personal rule: "You cannot do much in this world without life or death stakes. But if you dare to point a gun at someone, you should be prepared to be shot yourself." He uses firearms to create distance, interrupt an attack, or open an escape route. Mobility Motorcycle The only driving licence he ever wanted was for a motorcycle. He values the machine as a narrow, responsive escape tool that is harder to trap than a car, not as a leisure accessory. Last resort Survival combat Fights to remain mobile and alive, combining practical close combat with terrain awareness instead of pursuing elegant or decisive victories. Leadership peak Intelligence operations His unofficial MSF association gives him access to surveillance, counterintelligence, field planning, and institutional command. By Lynleit's disappearance, this becomes the side of MSF he has mastered completely. Kyrien

entries.subtitle: Demiholumn and Natalia's outside ally
entries.text: Lester: Biography Demiholumn and Natalia's outside ally Lester is a demiholumn, half human and half Holumn. The circumstances of his birth or transformation, and whether either description is fully accurate, remain unknown. He becomes Natalia's ally without becoming her employee. When one of her cases reaches an impossible barrier, his unusual nature can provide an answer that neither ordinary investigation nor conventional magecraft could reach. His existence gives Natalia access to possibilities that make her private work uniquely valuable, while also creating a secret that could become more dangerous than the case being investigated. He pushes against her examiner's distance and notices when her attention has become personal rather than clinical. His sexual tension with Natalia develops through repeated cases without resolving whether she can understand his nature without reducing him to it. The first central case that requires his intervention, the limits of his abilities, and the response of the Church or Magiarchy if he is discovered remain unresolved. Between Human and Holumn Natalia's Outside Ally The Impossible Favor A Nature without an Explanation Lester

entries.text: Lester: Connections Demiholumn and Natalia's outside ally Natalia Natalia is his trusted investigator ally, not his employer. She calls on him when a case crosses the boundary between difficult and impossible. Their attraction grows through his refusal to remain only an object of her analysis and her increasing ability to see the man without ignoring the demiholumn condition. Classification Any institution that reduces him to either a human witness or a Holumn threat will misunderstand what he is and may decide that he cannot be allowed to remain free. Potential sexual tension Natalia Established tension Mutual, differently expressed Natalia's analytical distance gives Lester something unusually difficult to provoke. He enjoys forcing the reserved researcher into immediate experience, but the tension changes when he wants her attention to recognize the man rather than examine the demiholumn condition. Their casework repeatedly joins Natalia's detached analysis to Lester's direct, embodied engagement with the impossible. She is drawn toward the part of him her research cannot settle. He pushes against being treated as a case and learns to distinguish her examiner's attention from personal interest. The tension belongs to that unstable boundary: Natalia must encounter him as a man without abandoning the questions his existence raises, while Lester wants to be understood without becoming legible enough to lose his freedom. entries.title: Lynleit: Biography
entries.subtitle: Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir
entries.text: Lynleit: Biography Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir Lynleit is Fionn's biological daughter and intended heir. Helena is her stepmother, not her biological mother. Raised close to MSF leadership, Lynleit inherits Fionn's blue-flame magecraft, while a childhood fear of drowning independently manifests as the forbidden ability to walk on water. Felix and Reiner are already her close, long-standing friends before the story begins, as well as the personal bodyguards Fionn trusts with her safety. Natalia was Lynleit's favourite teacher during her Magi Academy years. Her relationship with Helena is always tense. Before any open conspiracy, Lynleit notices Helena repeatedly probing details that seem domestic in isolation: Fionn's schedules, visitors to the house, officers he trusts, and Lynleit's own travel. She begins to suspect murder because somebody is studying her family too carefully. Within the first few chapters, Kyrien attacks a Magus politician under MSF protection and almost harms Lynleit during the failed attempt. She knows how close he came; he does not know she was present, and she never tells him. Lynleit later questions him with that private injury behind her authority, then uses an extraordinary transfer clause in MSF's government service contract to recruit him as her first deeply anti-protocol MSF decision. She eventually limits the truth to Felix and Reiner without informing even Fionn. Days before Fionn's death, the Nameless Street leaves Lynleit with the memory of a dead boy below a broken fence. When Fionn is later found below the hill at the family house, the resemblance stupefies her and allows Helena to give a false meaning to a genuine reaction. The still-unresolved conspiracy vindicates Lynleit's warning without implying that she foresaw its exact form. Helena takes control, frames Lynleit for his death, and directs a hunt for her arrest. Lynleit exhausts her available resources to escape and reaches Kyrien's hotel-room hideout, where her composure finally breaks. He later helps her establish contact with Felix and Reiner, beginning her slow effort to reclaim MSF while she remains hunted. Lynleit continues initiating Fionn's blue recognition sequence on the run. His most conservative old officers recognize the conversational response that Helena cannot give and begin to treat obedience to the founder's protocol as a reason to question his official successor. During the failed river watches, short card games after each aborted operation become Lynleit and Kyrien's first voluntary routine. She learns the stopped breath before one of his risks, while he learns the small hand movement before one of her decisions. The attraction produced by that attention remains involuntary for Lynleit and never outranks the operation. On the fifth watch, Kyrien briefly steadies her near the Sparrow holster when an empty boat shifts, then is driven toward the quarantined park bank when the Drowned Choir attacks. Reiner, Maren, and Ivo reach Felix on the city bank. The hands drag Lynleit underwater, tear away her fitted blue suede jacket, and trigger fury alongside her childhood fear of drowning. Her blue flame burns the hands even beneath the water. After she breaks the surface, it supports her palm, knee, and boots until she stands above hands that cannot cross the surface layer. Only Kyrien sees the forbidden act. Lynleit later reaches him inside the night park, where their awareness of each other's breathing continues while they sit back to back for warmth. His careful denial protects her secret. Father Mikhail later discovers that she has shared forbidden knowledge with Kyrien, Felix, and Reiner. Her refusal to surrender or suppress them begins the pressure to create a formal Magi role for MSF. During Father Mikhail's Arc 1 venture in Cardiff, the Magiarchy and Church send Lynleit to assist him. Abroad and without MSF or its conventional arsenal, she must rely on her Magus training. She and Mikhail continue protecting one another and completing their missions even after their morally incompatible methods become impossible to ignore. Before leaving Narvea, Lynleit answers Natalia's request by sending Kyrien to help Myka at the Academy in her place. She understates the danger and expects the assignment to teach him more about the Magi world. Lynleit later complains about losing the blue suede jacket because she liked it. Midway through Arc 1, after Fionn's death, she discovers that he had discreetly replaced her blue coat with a protective garment made from the hide of leviathan. The coat changes form by its own judgment and sometimes imitates the lost jacket, but protection requires Lynleit to use it actively rather than simply wear it. When Lynleit's authority over Kyrien can no longer compel him, he chooses to remain in the counteroffensive. Their relationship becomes sexual only at the end of Arc 1, after intimacy has accumulated inside their work through unfinished contests, practical care, danger, and voluntary loyalty. Lynleit disappears near the transition into Arc 2. The opening of Arc 2 supplies the circumstances from which her pregnancy can be inferred without showing or explaining it directly. She remains away to keep the child beyond the conflict's reach, recover, and consult wiser people about the Spill's origins. Years later she does not announce a return. She appears around MSF missions, sometimes seemingly by accident and sometimes by design, and her unexplained presence can make her look like a culprit. entries.title: Lynleit: Connections
entries.subtitle: Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir
entries.text: Lynleit: Connections Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir Natalia Former favourite teacher Natalia taught Lynleit at the Magi Academy, later asks her to help Myka, and identifies ego transformation as the survivable answer to the curse Lynleit shares with Kyrien. Father Mikhail Cardiff counterpart and theological adviser The Magiarchy and Church send Lynleit to assist Mikhail abroad. They protect one another despite a moral rift, and he later confirms through Church records that the shared curse can be broken through genuine identity transformation. Kyrien Their connection begins with concealed personal stakes: his attack on an MSF-protected politician nearly harms Lynleit, but Kyrien never learns she was present. She later coerces him into service and keeps him hidden even from Fionn. Card games after the failed river watches create their first voluntary rhythm, while the operation turns their attention to bodily tells and physical distance. Kyrien protects her water-walking secret and eventually chooses to remain after her authority can no longer compel him. Near the end of Arc 1, destroying a Holumn together binds one fatal curse to both identities. Lynleit rejects the solution that one must die, investigates transformation as an alternative, and initiates their first sexual encounter when the prognosis falls to days. Their reciprocal change fractures the curse. Attraction never outranks her duty to MSF. Helena Lynleit distrusts her stepmother before the takeover, then learns Helena played a major role in Fionn's assassination even though the full conspiracy remains unclear. Potential sexual tension Kyrien Established arc Mutual, slow to surface MSF and her personal missions remain Lynleit's priorities. Her attention to Kyrien begins as operational scrutiny, sharpened by the knowledge that his failed attempt nearly harmed her, and becomes involuntarily physical through the tells she learns during their repeated card games. His claim that a battle is reason enough to stay removes both obedience and promised reward from his persistence. She dislikes the distraction and returns to the work whenever it intrudes. When their shared curse forces a decision, she still approaches intimacy as a problem to investigate and a responsibility she must carry. Their attraction begins through observation rather than romance. The interrogation gives Lynleit private knowledge Kyrien cannot read. The failed river watches then give them a voluntary contest outside the handler-asset bargain: Lynleit learns the stopped breath before one of his risks, while he learns the hand movement before one of her decisions. Hands, breath, gaze, pauses, proximity, and competitive attention become their private language. The river recovery and the hotel refuge remain non-sexual thresholds in which restraint makes physical and emotional trust possible. Kyrien's choice to remain after Lynleit's authority loses practical force separates desire from compliance. When a shared Holumn curse later reduces their remaining time to days, Lynleit investigates intimacy as a possible identity change and initiates a clumsy, sudden, almost argumentative encounter. Kyrien understands what she is asking and answers deliberately. The curse does not create their attachment or make sex curative. It forces both to acknowledge a relationship already capable of changing the identities it recognizes. Potential sexual tension Felix Established asymmetry Felix overt, Lynleit deflecting Felix's flirting belongs to a long friendship she refuses to reorganize around his advances. Her ease with him, combined with the repeated refusal, creates visible chemistry without requiring matching sexual intent. The tension is easy for readers to recognize because it already has a social rhythm: he advances through jokes and flirtation, she ignores or redirects him, and neither abandons the closeness underneath the exchange. It does not need to become a relationship to remain real. Lynleit

entries.title: Lynleit: Magecraft
entries.subtitle: Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir
entries.text: Lynleit: Magecraft Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir Hereditary magecraft Blue flame Lynleit inherited her family's ability to manifest blue flame. It can be directed into many applications, but her control is less subtle than Fionn's. Natural tendency Unsafe volume Where Fionn relies on virtuosity and precision, Lynleit has the nerve to call forth far more flame than is safe. Force comes more readily to her than finesse. Irreplaceable force Beyond ordinary weapons Blue flame becomes indispensable when normal firearms cannot finish the threat: an immortal or rapidly regenerating Holumn, a body that moves without being alive, or a barrier that conventional force cannot breach. Accidental miracle-making Walking on water This ability was neither inherited nor taught. It manifested from her childhood fear of drowning and allows her to cross the surface of water on foot. Its resemblance to a sacred miracle places it outside tolerated magecraft. Strictly concealed Night practice Lynleit keeps the talent secret from everyone because the Church strongly punishes miracle-making that imitates acts associated with Jesus, saints, saviours, and other sacred figures, even when the effect seems harmless. She practices alone at night on secluded stretches of local lakes and rivers. Lynleit

entries.title: Lynleit: Strengths and weaknesses
entries.subtitle: Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir
entries.text: Lynleit: Strengths and weaknesses Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir Lynleit places MSF duty and her personal missions above private wants. She studies hidden structures with private precision, interprets present events through their future consequences, and builds contingencies around the people for whom she feels responsible. She treats openness as a leadership skill and normally gives people the truth they need to act with her. Under mortal pressure, she rejects solutions that sacrifice someone under her protection, searches across every available discipline, and acts decisively. Her concealment in Doom Has an Address is a narrow exception caused by the sexual and personally humiliating nature of the plan. Relational leadership 95 Her first instinct in crisis is to read trust, morale, legitimacy, shared burden, and the emotional field around her. She treats candid communication as a practical source of trust and coordinated action. Strategic foresight 92 Her unusually strong intuition identifies long-range patterns and what events are becoming before most people can name the change. Private introspection 86 In private she is comfortable disappearing into solitude, following symbolic threads, and processing difficult emotion internally. ENFJ strong Ni Confirmed Lynleit

entries.title: Myka: Biography
entries.subtitle: Magi Academy student
entries.text: Myka: Biography Magi Academy student Myka enters an Academy that functions as a public institution within Magi society. Magi families and lineages fund it so their children can succeed them, while acclaimed Magi who choose research and teaching serve as professors. Her aunt Natalia, a former professor and Lynleit's favourite teacher, remains a constant source of advice and a personal connection to life beyond the institution. Myka encounters terrors inside the Academy and must rely on Natalia for rescue and support. Natalia asks Lynleit for help, but Lynleit is being sent to Cardiff and dispatches Kyrien as her substitute. The threat turns formal study into a struggle for survival inside an institution meant to train and protect young Magi. Kyrien enters the Academy as a non-Magus undercover helper and keeps Myka safe through conventional field skills and communications with Felix and Reiner. The danger exceeds Lynleit's estimate and forces Natalia to intervene personally. This becomes Myka's first direct experience with Kyrien and MSF. Myka survives the Academy crisis and graduates at the top of her class. Her experience with Kyrien and MSF contributes to her later decision to join the agency as a strong Magus. Her recruitment most likely follows Lynleit's disappearance and Kyrien's assumption of the director's office, but that placement remains unresolved. entries.title: Natalia: Biography
entries.subtitle: Independent magical examiner and private investigator
entries.text: Natalia: Biography Independent magical examiner and private investigator Natalia earned a professorship at the Magi Academy as a talented Magus and serious researcher. Lynleit became her favourite student during those years. Natalia eventually found academic life too constraining: the institution could support scholarship, but it also defined which questions were respectable and how far an inquiry was permitted to go. She resigned to continue her work independently. Freedom did not finance itself. Natalia opened a private-investigation business as a practical source of income, then discovered that her immense knowledge of Magi and magecraft made her uniquely valuable to clients with cases no ordinary investigator could understand. Her one-woman office now sits between a detective agency, consultation room, and private laboratory. Clients bring suspected crimes, unstable talents, personal deviations, and magical problems they cannot safely expose. Natalia examines the person and phenomenon before deciding whether a crime has occurred at all. Lester repeatedly forces her to distinguish professional fascination with his demiholumn condition from personal attention to him. When Myka encounters terrors inside the Academy, Natalia becomes her principal source of advice, rescue, and support beyond the institution. She asks her former student Lynleit for help, then intervenes personally when the danger exceeds the protection Kyrien can provide. Her practice becomes highly sought after in the narrow interval before the Magiarchy or Church learns enough to claim a case. Her sexual tension with Lester develops through investigations that require her analysis and his direct engagement with the impossible. The Academy crisis renews Natalia's connection with Lynleit and brings Kyrien, Felix, Reiner, and MSF into Myka's life. entries.subtitle: Independent magical examiner and private investigator
entries.text: Natalia: Strengths and weaknesses Independent magical examiner and private investigator Natalia is a researcher first and a private investigator by necessity. She protects her intellectual autonomy, builds her own analytical framework, and studies unusual systems without needing institutional agreement. Under pressure, she moves between ritual history, psychology, folklore, and magecraft until one mechanism accounts for the evidence. She teaches by making the other person define the problem correctly before she supplies the conclusion, then permits herself dry humor once the analysis is secure. Independent scholarship She resigned from the Academy when its environment became too restrictive for the questions and methods she wanted to pursue. Magical examination She investigates people as readily as incidents, studying unusual magecraft, personal deviations, and conditions with a precision closer to a physician than a conventional detective. Selective casework The business has one employee: Natalia. Paid cases finance her research and let her choose which clients, risks, and secrets enter her office. Identity analysis When Lynleit and Kyrien inherit a curse across both egos, Natalia connects the mechanism to substitute identities, sympathetic recognition, and changes deep enough to reorganize the conscious self. entries.text: Reiner: Biography MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard Reiner serves as an MSF officer, but his place beside Lynleit is already personal long before the story begins. They are close friends, and Fionn regards Reiner as one of her reliable bodyguards. He therefore accompanies her on operations, travel, and casual outings where formal protection blends into ordinary company. Lynleit reveals her secret recruitment of Kyrien only to Reiner and Felix, withholding it even from Fionn. Reiner sees the same danger Felix sees, particularly whenever neither bodyguard is near her, but recognizes that rejecting the plan would also mean rejecting Lynleit's judgment. Despite being the more protocol-focused friend, Reiner concedes because he chooses to trust Lynleit's intuition. His decision leaves Felix in the minority and makes Reiner the stabilizing vote inside a compartment all three know violates MSF practice. Reiner's trust does not eliminate scrutiny. After Fionn's murder and the hunt for Lynleit's arrest, Kyrien helps her contact Reiner and Felix from hiding. Reiner must protect her, preserve the covert link inside Helena's MSF, and decide how far disciplined loyalty can support the effort to reclaim the agency. entries.text: Sherie: Biography Diplomat in training and covert negotiator Sherie trains under her uncle Drake to become a successful diplomat. Their age gap matters less than the complement between his strategic mind and her instinctive command of social atmosphere. Drake's peers ridicule his warning and the Duke remains skeptical. Sherie believes her uncle, but rejects his decision to remain inside official limits and begins designing her own approach to Lynleit. The illegal MSF partnership is entirely Sherie's idea and strategy. She develops it against Drake's wishes, persuades him to attend, and takes command of the negotiations. In this specific diplomatic test, the student surpasses her teacher. Once it succeeds, she asks Drake to praise and pamper her for her first achievement. Sherie and Drake use the private agreement to ask Lynleit for a loyal team capable of covertly inspecting apparently unmanned night shipments on the Vilen river. The empty boats and the Drowned Choir prove that the suspected coup cannot be understood as a purely political operation. Official oversight The government and Ducal Court would end the partnership if either discovered it. Potential sexual tension Kyrien Strong potential Situational and confrontational Kyrien's refusal to be steered threatens a skill she has internalized as part of her identity. Each failed attempt to produce a reaction can make his eventual attention feel more valuable and personally dangerous. Sherie uses language and calibrated flirtation to control the rhythm of an exchange. Kyrien answers with silence, literalism, or no usable reaction at all. Repeated negotiation could turn her professional frustration into sexual tension without making them compatible or displacing Kyrien's eventual relationship with Lynleit. Potential sexual tension Felix Emerging potential Mutual play, sincerity unresolved Felix gives Sherie immediate wit, visible attention, and resistance that does not become hostility. She first tests him as play and competition, including whether his attention can be drawn away from Lynleit. The tension becomes personal when winning ceases to satisfy her and she begins wanting a response that is not produced by technique. Both use social ease as protection: Felix hides seriousness behind jokes, while Sherie hides vulnerability behind charm and diplomacy. Their chemistry is immediate, but similarity makes them capable of prolonged flirtation without honest movement. Sherie begins testing the friendship after learning that Lynleit has slept with Kyrien while still feeling responsible for Felix's affection. Her refusal to treat Felix as Lynleit's permanent responsibility creates a comic rivalry with Lynleit and a more serious test of whether Sherie wants Felix himself or only wants to win his attention. entries.title: Yulia: Biography
entries.subtitle: Criminology student and procedural investigator
entries.text: Yulia: Biography Criminology student and procedural investigator Yulia and Hiyu study criminology at the same university. She stands at the top of the class through discipline, detail, and command of established method, while Hiyu makes his reputation through personal investigations that ignore the path everyone else was taught to follow. Their interaction is often painful to observe: he chases another possibility, she develops another headache, and neither notices how accustomed they are becoming to the other's company. Hiyu concludes that magic may be involved in the park disappearances despite not knowing that magic actually exists. Yulia considers the theory absurd, but joins his attempt to enter the quarantine partly to prove him wrong and partly because she does not trust him to remain safe alone. Inside the park, Yulia's meticulous observation remains valuable, but ordinary criminological protocol cannot tell her what rules the environment follows. Her attachment to Hiyu becomes a second vulnerability because protecting him can pull her deeper into a danger neither of them understands. Their original aversion gradually becomes dependence and then unacknowledged romantic tension. Yulia refuses to name it, while Hiyu remains so absorbed in ideas that he does not understand why her company has become necessary to him. Top of the Class Dragged into the Park Proof without Protocol Addicted to the Contrast Yulia

entries.text: Yulia: Connections Criminology student and procedural investigator Hiyu Her opposite in method and temperament. He generates possibilities she would never entertain, while she gives his ideas evidentiary discipline. Over time, irritation becomes an attachment neither understands clearly. An investigation without rules Yulia can master a known procedure, but the park confronts her with evidence whose governing categories have not yet been admitted to exist. Potential sexual tension Hiyu Emerging arc Mutual, unequally conscious Hiyu irritates her into sustained attention. She keeps arguing, correcting, and following because his ideas have already occupied more of her mind than she wants to admit. Suppressed attraction can sharpen both her impatience and her awareness of his physical presence. Their arguments repeatedly force proximity and attention. They lean over the same evidence, reach for the same document, and forget ordinary distance while trying to prove incompatible explanations. Yulia notices first and steps away; Hiyu continues the theory and wonders why she moved. Her anger becomes disproportionate when his recklessness makes the possibility of losing him real. Hiyu recognizes the bond through absence: an investigation without her corrections becomes less interesting, and he keeps turning toward the place where she should be. Yulia and Hiyu become intimate by learning to communicate through the noise they already create together. Yulia

entries.title: Yulia: Strengths and weaknesses
entries.subtitle: Criminology student and procedural investigator
entries.text: Yulia: Strengths and weaknesses Criminology student and procedural investigator Yulia is methodical, detail-oriented, reliable, and most comfortable when evidence can be tested against a stable procedure. Hiyu's constant eureka moments and improvised logic give her a headache, but she repeatedly follows him anyway. Their opposition works because she checks what he leaps toward, while he forces her to consider possibilities no established protocol would admit. Procedural rigor She is at the top of her criminology class because she applies method consistently, respects chains of evidence, and notices when a required step has been skipped. Detail verification Yulia is strongest when a theory must be tested against the record, an observation must be preserved accurately, or an exciting conclusion must survive patient scrutiny. Reluctant loyalty She complains, resists, and wishes she were elsewhere, yet still goes with Hiyu when leaving him alone would place him in greater danger. ISTJ strong Si Confirmed Yulia

entries.title: Yulia: Tradecraft
entries.subtitle: Criminology student and procedural investigator
entries.text: Yulia: Tradecraft Criminology student and procedural investigator Academic strength Classical criminological method Yulia follows evidence handling, observation, reconstruction, and procedural discipline with a consistency Hiyu does not naturally possess. Team function Verification and correction She tests Hiyu's intuitive threads, separates useful anomalies from noise, and gives their investigations a record another person could actually follow. Failure condition Procedure without precedent The quarantined park is especially dangerous because its supernatural conditions do not respect the categories or safety assumptions on which her strongest methods depend. Yulia
